en: Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the floor, preventing you from slipping and falling on wet tiles.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water conducts electricity and can cause a dangerous shock.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light and prevents long-term damage to your eyes.
Wearing earplugs at loud events protects the delicate hair cells in your inner ear from permanent hearing loss.
Using thick oven mitts when holding hot pots slows down heat transfer and prevents severe skin burns.
Using an inclined plane like a ramp to move heavy boxes prevents back injuries caused by lifting.
Unplugging appliances by pulling the hard plug instead of the cord prevents internal wires from breaking and causing fires.
Eating carbohydrate-rich foods like rice provides your body with chemical energy needed to fuel your brain and muscles at school.
Keep strong neodymium magnets away from smartphones to prevent them from damaging the phone's internal electronic compass.
Always hold heavy backpacks close to your body to keep your center of gravity low and prevent falling backward.
Rubbing your hands together quickly generates thermal energy through friction, which helps warm your body during cold rainy days.
Using a wheelbarrow to transport heavy soil uses the lever and wheel-and-axle to prevent muscle strain in your arms.
